Properties of a naxp

Source: R/naxp.R
naxp_properties.Rd

The pattern a naxp was parsed from, its largest encoded value, the length of its longest canonical form, and the naxp an encoded vector carries.

Usage

naxp_pattern(naxp)

naxp_max_encoded_value(naxp)

naxp_max_length(naxp)

naxp_of(x)

Arguments

naxp

A naxp from naxp_parse(), or a pattern string.

x

A naxp_encoded vector.

Value

  • naxp_pattern(): a single string.

  • naxp_max_encoded_value(): a single integer or double.

  • naxp_max_length(): a single integer.

  • naxp_of(): a naxp.

Details

Encoded values run from 1 to the maximum with no gaps, so the maximum is also the number of distinct encoded values. It is an integer where it is at most 2^31 - 1 and a double where it is at most 2^53. Above 2^53, which is the largest whole number R holds exactly, naxp_max_encoded_value() raises an error, although printing the naxp still shows the maximum.

Examples

nl_postcode <- naxp_parse(r"(\9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A)")
naxp_pattern(nl_postcode)
#> [1] "\\9\\9\\9\\9 \\s!! \\A\\A"
naxp_max_encoded_value(nl_postcode)
#> [1] 6760000
naxp_max_length(nl_postcode)
#> [1] 7

codes <- naxp_encode(c("1012AB", "9999 ZZ"), nl_postcode)
naxp_of(codes)
#> <naxp> \9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A
#> Maximum encoded value: 6760000
